(CNN) -- Chester Arthur Stiles, his wrists and ankles bound in restraints and his lengthy hair partially hiding his features, made his first appearance before a Las Vegas, Nevada court on Wednesday morning. The 37-year-old faces charges connected to a video recording that captured the rape of a toddler.

Authorities apprehended Stiles on Monday evening when a Henderson police officer stopped the white Buick Century he was operating. By Wednesday's hearing, prosecutors had tacked on additional charges, pushing the total count to 23 felonies. These included lewd conduct with a minor, sexual assault, and creating child pornography, according to Clark County court documents. Court officials noted that one lewdness charge dated back to an incident in 2004, while the remaining charges connected to the videotaped assault.

Judge Deborah Lippis scheduled the preliminary hearing for November 19. Following the proceeding, Stiles' court-appointed defender indicated his client seemed shaken by the intense public scrutiny surrounding the case. "I think he's a little out of it," said public defender Jeff Banks.

According to Jerry T. Donohue, who represents the victim's mother, the child depicted in the video was under three years old at the time of the abuse. The girl, now seven, was located last month following an extensive nationwide search effort.

Speaking on "The Dr. Phil Show" Wednesday, the girl's mother expressed relief over Stiles' capture, though she admitted she would have preferred finding him dead. She confirmed her intention to testify should the case proceed to trial. In her conversation with host Phil McGraw, she revealed that her daughter has no memory of the recorded assault. She had recently discussed inappropriate touching with the child, who assured her mother she would scream and report any such incident.

Despite this reassurance, the mother confessed her trust in others has been shattered. Even though she's currently involved with a man the girl refers to as "Dad," she admitted discomfort leaving her daughter alone with him or anyone else. "I just cry and blame it on myself," she said. Now eight-and-a-half months into her pregnancy, she described the emotional toll the situation has taken on her, stating she would have preferred remaining unaware of what happened to her daughter.

A woman who once dated Stiles described living in terror after she went to authorities to identify him following the release of enhanced video images on local news broadcasts. Elaine Thomas told CNN's Nancy Grace that she's experienced numerous nightmares since then. Upon spotting the televised photos, she recalled screaming and feeling compelled to alert police, despite having previously viewed the man as merely a "weapons enthusiast" with a minimal criminal history.

"How could I not tell them who that man was? That little girl suffered unimaginable things, and I knew for a fact it was him," Thomas explained.

Tina Allen, another former girlfriend, revealed earlier this month her belief that she inadvertently connected Stiles with the young victim, expressing horror over the accusations. She explained her attraction to Stiles stemmed from his claims of Navy service, as she sought a masculine role model for her sons.

Allen recounted bringing Stiles to a densely populated apartment complex where her children resided alongside a family friend and that woman's daughter—who would later become the alleged victim. Todd Allen, her son, stated he identified his former residence from footage shown in the video.

*CNN's Ed Payne and Ted Rowlands contributed to this report.*
